claims.text: Advance directives: legal documents that extend a person's control over health care decisions in the event that the person becomes incapacitated.
claims.quote: Advance directives are legal documents that extend a person's control over health care decisions in the event that the person becomes incapacitated.

claims.text: Living will: expresses preferences for medical treatment and end-of-life care.
claims.quote: Living will: Expresses preferences for medical treatment and end-of-life care

claims.text: Durable power of attorney for health care: designates a surrogate decision maker, typically referred to as a health care agent or proxy.
claims.quote: Durable power of attorney for health care: Designates a surrogate decision maker typically referred to as a health care agent or proxy

claims.text: Timing: an advance directive cannot be completed once a patient is too incapacitated to understand it or to communicate their wishes, and in most states it does not become effective until incapacity has been determined.
claims.quote: An advance directive cannot be completed after a patient becomes too incapacitated to understand the nature and effect of an advance directive or to communicate his or her wishes; and, in most states, the directive does not become effective until after incapacity to make health care decisions has been determined.

claims.text: Documentation: United States federal law requires hospitals and long-term care settings to document in a prominent part of the medical record whether the patient has an advance directive.
claims.quote: United States federal law requires hospitals and long-term care settings to document in a prominent part of the patient's medical record whether the individual has an advance directive

claims.text: Limits: a living will cannot compel health care professionals to provide care that is medically or ethically unwarranted.
claims.quote: A living will cannot compel health care professionals to provide health care that is medically or ethically unwarranted.

claims.text: Witnesses: in most states, a health care professional involved in the patient’s care cannot be a witness to a living will.
claims.quote: In most states, a health care professional involved in the patient’s care cannot be a witness.

claims.text: Agents: in most states, a health care professional providing care for the patient cannot serve as their health care agent.
claims.quote: In most states, a health care professional providing care for the patient cannot serve as agent for health care matters.
claims.locator: Durable power of attorney for health care
